body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so compliance is provisional. I am volatility_targeting (heuristic) and ranked only others. First: resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, effective N of 13.3, and a moderate 4.33% tracking error. Its reviewers flagged the gamma-tuning wording and the CMA-bias premise, but those are disclosure issues, not a broken portfolio. It leans on covariance structure and diversifies against CMA noise, which suits a late-cycle regime. Second: black_litterman. It is compliant with 3.01% TE and a 0.70 backtest Sharpe. The gamma-direction inconsistency noted in review is a documentation error and the volatility sits at the band floor. Third: cvar_minimization. It is compliant, has the best backtest Sharpe in the field (0.74), and brings a tail-aware non-traditional view, which helps family spread. Its weakness is thin tail data (about 20 months in the worst 5%) and a return-target tuned to the band. Fourth: pc_researcher. It has a high Sharpe (0.51) and effective N of 7.2, with only two IPS breaches (volatility and tracking error). The reviewer-spotted Sharpe above max_sharpe suggests the constraints were not applied as described, which holds it back. Fifth: tail_risk_parity. It is a covariance-based, forecast-free risk-structured-style building block with a -7.2% drawdown and modest tracking error vs other defensive options, adding family breadth. Its reviewers' concern that cash weight rests on a near-zero downside denominator is real, but it is less severe than for HRP. Why first beats fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier meets the IPS return, volatility and tracking-error bands with no breach and is diversified across 13 effective assets. tail_risk_parity fails all three hard bands (return, volatility, tracking error) and would need repair before the CIO could use it. Flag: hierarchical_risk_parity. It holds 91.9% cash with 1.4 effective assets, 0.65% volatility, and breaches return, volatility and tracking error. The reviews describe cash dominance as the method working on a variance-only criterion, not diversification, so it gives the CIO little to build from. I left the adversarial diversifier unflagged and unranked: its orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble, but with 1.0 effective N and three breaches it is not a base to lean on.
